title: Automation Anywhere Alternatives: 6 Options and What AA Really Costs
summary: Compare six Automation Anywhere alternatives, including Skyvern, UiPath, and Power Automate. Explore features, pricing, and business workflow use cases.
body_markdown:
If you’re looking for an Automation Anywhere alternative, you’re probably unhappy with something: the price, a workflow builder that feels clunky, or the effort it takes to keep your automations running.


Those frustrations show up in Automation Anywhere’s reviews. Some reviewers describe expensive licensing, costs that become harder to predict as AI usage grows, and a steep learning curve for complex workflows. Others point to difficult debugging and resource-heavy deployments.


A lot of the people we talk to at Skyvern are coming from expensive, outdated Automation Anywhere setups. They wonder whether they still need such a costly, complicated setup for the work they actually do.


If it’s your case and you are trying to automate business workflows that happen in the browser, then Skyvern is built for that work. Downloading invoices, filling out forms, and updating customer or supplier portals are exactly the workflows we designed it to automate.


In this article, we compare 6 Automation Anywhere alternatives, including Skyvern. We explain what each does, and cover the pricing and tradeoffs when switching.


## 6 Automation Anywhere alternatives


Alternative Primary scope Pricing model


**Skyvern** Browser workflows owned by operations teams Cloud subscriptions with credits; custom Enterprise

*Updated on October 24, 2026. Dollar amounts below are USD.*


## Automation Anywhere: what it is and what it costs


Automation Anywhere combines RPA, AI agents, and document processing to automate work across web, desktop, and legacy applications. Teams build bots that move data between systems, process documents, and complete repetitive tasks. Attended bots work alongside employees; unattended bots run independently. A central Control Room manages access, schedules jobs, and monitors execution.


The[Cloud Starter Pack](https://www.automationanywhere.com/company/blog/product-insights/why-cloud-why-rpa-as-a-service?ref=skyvern.com) launched in 2020 at **$750/month ($9,000/year)** , including one Bot Creator, one Control Room, and one unattended Bot Runner. Additional bot capacity, implementation, infrastructure, and ongoing maintenance increase the total cost.


## 1. Skyvern — for business workflows in the browser


We built Skyvern for the business work that happens in a browser: signing into supplier portals, downloading invoices, filling out forms, and updating records. This is what we do best, and it’s why we’re putting Skyvern first on this list.


We want the people who understand the process to have a hand in automating it. With our[no-code builder](https://www.skyvern.com/products) , you can arrange the steps visually, describe the task in plain English, or upload your existing procedure through **SOP Upload** . We bring navigation, logins, data extraction, loops, and file handling together in the same workflow.


We also built the features around the task: saved credentials, recurring schedules, run recordings, and action logs. For monthly invoice collection, that means your team can set the accounts and date range, schedule the job, and review what happened during each run. These recurring operational processes are exactly what we built Skyvern for.


Our focus is browser automation. We don’t automate native desktop applications, SAP GUI, or mainframe clients. So if this is what you need, then another alternative will be a better fit.


Our[Skyvern Cloud plans](https://www.skyvern.com/pricing) start with a free plan containing 5,000 credits. We offer Hobby at $29/month with 30,000 monthly credits and Pro at $149/month with 150,000. Enterprise pricing is custom, and features such as team workspaces, 2FA support, and human review vary by plan.


[Try Skyvern for free](https://www.skyvern.com/pricing) ***and build your first workflow for collecting invoices, filling out forms, or updating supplier portals.***


## 2. UiPath


UiPath automates tasks across desktop software, websites, and older business applications. Its[UI automation](https://www.uipath.com/platform/agentic-automation/rpa?ref=skyvern.com) also supports virtual environments such as Citrix, giving it broad coverage for an enterprise RPA program.


Studio combines a visual workflow designer, reusable components, and code. Autopilot can generate workflows from natural-language instructions. Orchestrator manages deployment and monitoring, with execution records for investigating failures.


The platform covers both building automations and managing them across a business. Like Automation Anywhere, it requires people to develop, test, and maintain those workflows. Moving to UiPath changes the tools; the responsibility for operating the automations stays with your team.


UiPath pricing starts at $25/month for the limited Basic plan. Standard and Enterprise require a quote covering users, robot capacity, and usage allowances.


## 3. Microsoft Power Automate


Power Automate connects Microsoft 365, Dynamics, and other business applications. Cloud flows move data and trigger actions through connectors. Desktop flows interact with application interfaces, including older software without a useful API.


An approval workflow connects a request in SharePoint to an approval in Teams and an update in the destination system. Microsoft provides templates, a visual flow designer, and Copilot assistance for building these workflows, along with integrations for Excel, Teams, and SharePoint.


The licensing separates attended automation, which runs alongside a user, from unattended automation, which runs independently.


Microsoft’s US pricing lists Premium at $15/user/month, Process at $150/bot/month for unattended automation, and Hosted Process at $215/bot/month with a Microsoft-hosted virtual machine. All three prices are paid yearly.


## 4. SS&C Blue Prism


SS&C Blue Prism gives automation teams central control over processes running across departments and applications. Its Enterprise platform interacts with legacy and modern software and records automation activity in audit trails.


The wider product range includes managed cloud deployment, automation on employees’ desktops, and Chorus for coordinating business processes. Together, these products address the automated tasks, human work, and oversight involved in a larger automation program.


Blue Prism serves the same broad enterprise category as Automation Anywhere. Its central controls support an automation team responsible for process design, deployment, monitoring, and maintenance.


[Blue Prism pricing](https://www.blueprism.com/plans-pricing/?ref=skyvern.com) is quote-based, with costs determined by the products, deployment, capacity, and support in the package. The public pricing page lists the available products and editions without a universal production starting price.


## 5. Pega


Pega combines workflow automation, business rules, and case management. It organizes processes such as insurance claims and service requests into stages, decisions, and assignments, keeping track of the work as it moves between people and systems.


Its robotics tools cover attended bots that assist employees and unattended bots that run in the background. Robot Studio provides the development environment, while Robot Manager manages work queues and monitors bot performance.


Pega’s role extends beyond replacing individual AA bots. It brings the surrounding case, rules, employee tasks, and automated steps into one process model. That makes it a broader process-management investment.


Pega prices the required platform and robotics capabilities through a scoped quote. Its public RPA page does not list a starting price. Request separate figures for licensing, hosting, implementation, and support.


## 6. Workato


Workato automates processes across CRM, finance, support, and other business applications. It connects those systems through integrations and APIs, addressing the data-transfer work often handled by AA bots.


Its workflows, called **recipes** , start with an event and run a sequence of actions. Recipes can branch, process lists, call other recipes, and handle errors. For an onboarding recipe, use a new sale as the trigger, then create the billing account and notify the onboarding team.


These integrations move work between systems without reproducing a person’s clicks. Workato also lists RPA as an optional enterprise add-on. Desktop and legacy-interface automation therefore needs its own product scope and cost comparison.


Workato’s self-service Pro plan starts at $75/month for 2,500 credits.[Enterprise editions](https://www.workato.com/pricing?ref=skyvern.com) use negotiated terms and usage-based charges. The final bill reflects the capabilities included and the credits consumed by the workload.


## Frequently asked questions


### What are the top alternatives to Automation Anywhere?


This comparison covers Skyvern, UiPath, Microsoft Power Automate, SS&C Blue Prism, Pega, and Workato. Their scopes range from browser workflows to desktop RPA, case management, and application integrations. They do not all replace the same parts of an AA deployment.


### Which vendors offer a reliable, lower-cost alternative to Automation Anywhere?


Skyvern publishes Cloud pricing for browser workflows, starting with a free plan and paid tiers from $29/month. Microsoft also publishes per-user and per-bot prices. Those plans cover different capabilities.


### UiPath, Automation Anywhere, or a lighter tool: what fits a $50 million company with no RPA team?


Start with the workflow and identify who will own it. We built Skyvern for browser workflows managed by business teams, with a visual builder and SOP Upload. Desktop and legacy-system automation involves a broader scope. AA, UiPath, and other[UiPath alternatives](https://www.skyvern.com/blog/best-ai-native-alternative-uipath/) have different development, deployment, and support requirements.
